# A call that writes back is a statement's: made where it may not run, or may
# run again, there is no one place to write what it hands back. And a function
# that writes back is not a value, since what calls a value cannot know where
# its argument came from.

! sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out conditional.sngl
stderr 'conditional.sngl:17:26: pop writes "this" back where this call passed it, and it is made where it may not run, or may run again: call it in a statement of its own'

! sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out value.sngl
stderr 'value.sngl:17:13: fill writes "s", which a call hands back to the place it passed; taken as a value, nothing knows that place'

-- conditional.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Stack {
    items list[int] = []

    func pop() int {
        var top = this.items[0]
        this.items.remove(0)
        return top
    }
}

ui.window {
    var st = Stack{items=[1, 2]}
    var ok = false
    ui.button(text="x", @click {
        ok = ok && st.pop() > 0
    })
}
-- value.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Stack {
    items list[int] = []

    func add(x int) {
        this.items.push(x)
    }
}

func fill(s ref[Stack]) {
    s.add(1)
}

ui.window {
    var st = Stack{}
    var f = fill
    ui.button(text="x", @click {
        f(&st)
    })
}
